title: Canonical affine tilde tensor comparison is bijective on stalks
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, X = Spec R [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and M,N be R-modules. Write tilde M, tilde N, tilde(M tensor_R N) and tau for the associated module sheaves and their canonical maps on global sections [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Form the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with pure section tensors given by the sheafification map. If an O_X-linear morphism alpha : tilde(M tensor_R N) -> tilde M tensor_O_X tilde N sends tau(m tensor n) to tau(m) tensor tau(n) on global sections for every m,n, then for every x in X its induced map on module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is bijective.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8(1), second proof; verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I8

proof.text: For x with prime p, let S = R minus p and A = O_X,x. A is a localization of R at S. The maps f,g,q from M,N,M tensor_R N to their tilde stalks are module localization maps. Use the R-module structures of Mathlib tilde.toStalk; the scalar tower over A follows from the definition of its action.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8(1), second proof; verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I8

proof.text: TensorProduct.map f g is a module localization map at S. Compose with the inverse of IsLocalization.moduleTensorEquiv S A to obtain the localization map v : M tensor_R N -> M_x tensor_A N_x. The equivalence is the identity on pure tensors.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8(1), second proof; verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I8

proof.text: Use stalkTensorIso to identify the target stalk with M_x tensor_A N_x, by an A-linear equivalence psi. Set h = psi composed with alpha_x and restrict its scalars to R. Naturality of germs, the hypothesis on pure global tensors and the germ formula for stalkTensorIso imply h composed with q = v. TensorProduct.ext extends this equality from pure tensors to the entire module.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8(1), second proof; verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I8

proof.text: Since q and h composed with q are localization maps at S, IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv_of_isLocalizedModule_comp identifies h with the linear equivalence between those two localizations. Thus h is bijective, and cancelling the bijective psi proves alpha_x bijective.
